description: Cross-language contract for F-048/F-056: bank/UPI/card SMS -> expected classification and parse. 'expect' was produced by running the REAL Swift desktop TransactionParser / SmsClassifier / PatternPack.category (HaloTests ExpenseFixtureTests re-checks it); the Kotlin port (android/halocloud ExpenseFixtureTest) must agree. The one sanctioned difference is expect.classifierKotlin: the Kotlin classifier is pack-driven (full classifier lists) while the desktop's is a compact hard-coded port, so two messages classify differently; the Kotlin test insists every such message is a notTransaction on the parse side, so a classifier divergence can never create or hide a transaction. Where the desktop does something questionable it is recorded as-is with a 'note' - fix desktop and fixture together, never one alone. All messages are synthetic (no real account data).

messages.body: A/C *XX3833 debited by Rs 1250.00 via UPI. Avl Bal:8420.10 -IndusInd
messages.note: Category is 'Transfers' only because the body contains the word UPI (the Transfers rule triggers on UPI/IMPS/NEFT/RTGS in the body) - any unrecognised-merchant UPI debit lands in Transfers. Transfers is a label; only isTransfer (same-day debit+credit) excludes from totals.

messages.note: Desktop classifier says service (ORDER). The pack's broader transactionalStrong list has REFUND, so a pack-driven classifier says transactional; the parser then rejects it (INITIATED). Pipeline result is identical, so the Kotlin test pins pipeline behaviour for it. The Kotlin port classifies it from the pack (transactional, via REFUND) and the Swift desktop from its compact lists (service): see expect.classifierKotlin. Harmless - it is not a transaction either way.

messages.body: hey sent you Rs 500 for dinner, check
messages.note: Parser alone accepts it (a 'sent' verb + Rs); it is the classifier (sender is a bare phone number => Personal) that keeps it out of the pipeline. The cross-language contract is the pipeline: classifier gate then parse.

messages.body: Recharge of Rs 299 successful. Validity 28 days
messages.note: Classifier divergence (non-transactional both ways): the pack's promoKeywords include RECHARGE so the pack-driven Kotlin classifier says promotional; the Swift desktop's compact promo list lacks it, so it falls to the -S DLT suffix and says service. See expect.classifierKotlin. Neither feeds the expense pipeline.

messages.body: Payment of Rs 12,400 received towards your HDFC Bank Credit Card XX9981. Thank you
messages.note: DESKTOP QUIRK: 'Payment of Rs 12,400 received towards your credit card' is a debit - 'PAYMENT OF' is a debit verb and appears before 'RECEIVED'. It is the user paying their card bill, so a debit is defensible, but it is a settled bill and not a purchase.
